dataFields.name: Scheduled for
dataFields.validation: When the count is to be taken. Counts are periodic, not occasional (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Counted by
dataFields.validation: Who took the count. Never the storekeeper the count is checking (BR-2).

dataFields.name: System quantity
dataFields.validation: What the system says is on hand, at the moment the count is taken (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Counted quantity
dataFields.validation: What was physically on the shelf, in the item's own unit. Zero or more (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Difference
dataFields.validation: Counted less system. Negative where less was found than the system says (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Reason
dataFields.validation: 10 to 500 characters per difference. Required on every adjustment (BR-4).
dataFields.example: Three markers were taken for the parents' evening and never recorded.

dataFields.name: Direction
dataFields.validation: Whether the adjustment increases or decreases the balance.

dataFields.name: Source
dataFields.validation: What produced the adjustment. A count, or a damaged return from an issue.

dataFields.name: Return reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required to return an adjustment unapproved.
dataFields.example: Recount the stationery cupboard before this is approved.

businessRules.rule: A count is scheduled and taken periodically. It is not optional: physical stock never matches the system, since items are taken unrecorded, damaged, expired or quietly removed, and without a count the balance drifts until nobody trusts it and the whole module becomes dead weight.
The count is taken by somebody other than the storekeeper. A storekeeper counting their own store is checking their own work, which is not a check.
Counted quantities are entered against the system balances and the differences are shown, in each item's own unit.
An adjustment is raised for each difference, carrying a reason. A difference with no explanation is a difference nobody investigated.
The adjustment is approved before the balance changes, and the approval is recorded. The balance does not move on the counter's say-so.
The system quantity is taken at the moment the count is taken, so an issue recorded while the count is in progress does not appear as a difference.
A count covers every item in its scope, and an item left uncounted is reported as uncounted rather than as matching.
A damaged or unusable returnable item returned from an issue raises an adjustment through this route, with the reason carried from the return.
An adjustment is never deleted, and neither is a count. A wrong adjustment is corrected by a further adjustment.
An adjustment made outside a count is possible where a known error must be corrected, and carries the same reason and the same approval.
Repeated differences on the same item are visible together, since a shelf that is short every count is not an accident.

transitions.condition: Every item in scope is counted or reported uncounted (BR-7).
An adjustment with a reason is raised for each difference (BR-4).
Every adjustment is approved or returned (BR-5).
Approved. The balance changes now and not before (BR-5).
Returned with a reason. The balance is unchanged.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inventory → Stock counts → Schedule a count
basicFlow.userAction: Schedules the count, which is taken periodically rather than when somebody thinks of it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the count as due. It is not optional.

basicFlow.userAction: Takes the count, being somebody other than the storekeeper.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses where the counter is the storekeeper being counted against.

basicFlow.navigation: Take the count → Enter counted quantity
basicFlow.userAction: Enters what was physically on the shelf for each item, in that item's own unit.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the counted quantity against the system quantity taken at the moment the count began.

basicFlow.navigation: Take the count → Submit the count
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows every difference, and reports any item left uncounted as uncounted rather than as matching.

basicFlow.navigation: Differences and adjustments → Enter a reason → Raise adjustments
basicFlow.userAction: Raises an adjustment for each difference, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a reason on every adjustment.
Changes the balance now and not before, and records the approval.
Records the adjustment with its item, direction, quantity, reason, source and approver, and shows repeated differences on an item together.

alternateFlows.condition: The storekeeper attempts to take the count
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. A storekeeper counting their own store is checking their own work (BR-2).

alternateFlows.navigation: Take the count → Not yet counted
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is reported as uncounted rather than as matching, since an uncounted item is not a confirmed one (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept an adjustment
alternateFlows.navigation: Differences and adjustments → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns with a reason and the balance is unchanged (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: A returnable item came back damaged
alternateFlows.navigation: Inventory → Issues → Record a return → Damaged
alternateFlows.behaviour: An adjustment is raised through this route with the reason carried from the return, rather than the balance rising by an item nobody can use (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A known error must be corrected outside a count
alternateFlows.behaviour: An adjustment is raised with the same reason and the same approval as one from a count (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The same item is short at every count
alternateFlows.behaviour: The differences are visible together, since a shelf short every count is not an accident (BR-11).

departures.aspect: The counter is never the storekeeper
departures.requirement: There is no route by which the person responsible for the store takes the count of it. A storekeeper counting their own store is checking their own work.

departures.aspect: The balance moves only on approval
departures.requirement: No count, and no counter, changes a stock balance. Only an approved adjustment does.

departures.aspect: The count sheet hides the system figure
departures.requirement: The printed count sheet shows no system quantity, so the counter counts what is there rather than confirming what they were told.
An item left uncounted is reported as uncounted everywhere, and is never treated as agreeing with the system.

departures.aspect: Frozen at the moment of counting
departures.requirement: The system quantity is captured when the count begins, so movements during the count do not appear as differences.
Counts and adjustments are retained 7 years, since they explain every movement the balance cannot otherwise account for.

openQuestions.question: How often is a count taken — monthly, per term, or annually?
openQuestions.assumption: Periodic as modelled. The period is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Does every count cover every item, or does the school count by category in rotation?
openQuestions.assumption: Scope is settable as modelled but the school's practice is not stated.

openQuestions.question: Should a large difference require the Principal rather than the School Admin to approve?
openQuestions.assumption: Not modelled. There is one approver regardless of size.

openQuestions.question: Does an adjustment post to the ledger as a write-off of stock, or only change the quantity?
openQuestions.assumption: Only the quantity as modelled. Accounts see it but nothing posts.

openQuestions.question: What happens where a count reveals a large unexplained shortfall — is there any further process?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The adjustment is approved and the matter closes.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
